title: JAMB Use of English Mock Exam
subject: Use of English

questions.q: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The students _____ their assignments on time.'
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'submitted' because it's the past tense form that agrees with the subject 'students'.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of 'quickly' in 'She quickly finished her homework.'
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' is an adverb because it modifies the verb 'finished' by describing how the action was performed.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: 'Neither John nor his friends _____ going to the party.'
questions.explanation: When using 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Since 'friends' is plural, we use 'are'.

questions.q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'break the ice'?
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' means to start a conversation or make people feel comfortable in a social situation.

questions.q: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to 'generous':
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'generous' (willing to give or share) is 'selfish' (concerned only with oneself).

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech in 'The wind whispered through the trees.'
questions.explanation: This is personification because the wind (a non-human thing) is given human characteristics (whispering).
The correct spelling is 'accommodate' with double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.q: What is the plural form of 'criterion'?
questions.explanation: The plural form of 'criterion' is 'criteria' (from Greek origin).

questions.q: Choose the word that best fits: 'The _____ of the novel was very complex.'
questions.explanation: The correct word is 'plot' which refers to the main story or sequence of events in a novel.

questions.q: Identify the type of sentence: 'What a beautiful day!'
questions.explanation: This is an exclamatory sentence because it expresses strong emotion and ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: 'She is good _____ mathematics.'
questions.explanation: We use 'at' with 'good' when referring to skills or subjects: 'good at mathematics'.
To procrastinate means to delay or postpone doing something, especially something unpleasant.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: 'The book _____ on the table.'
questions.explanation: The correct form is 'lies' because it's the present tense of 'to lie' (to be in a horizontal position).

questions.q: Identify the literary device: 'Life is a journey.'
questions.explanation: This is a metaphor because it directly compares life to a journey without using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.q: Choose the word that means the same as 'enormous':
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' means very large or huge, so 'huge' is the synonym.
